event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: FRT’s 2023-02-08 Form 10-K links the COVID-19 pandemic to multiple vectors of risk that remain current and material less than three years after the WHO declaration.  The filing moves beyond boiler-plate by tying the pandemic to concrete revenue threats (tenant rent abatements, vacancy-driven cash-flow declines), operational delays (project completions slowed by supply-chain blockages and labor shortages), strategic uncertainty (shifts in demand for retail and office space) and organisational strain (remote-work impacts, cyber-attack exposure).  Although some statements are framed as possibilities, the MD&A acknowledges that 2022 cash-flows were “negatively impacted,” confirming an existing, not merely potential, hit.  The document also details partial mitigants—rent deferrals, increased liquidity, improving collections—which temper but do not eliminate the exposure.  Given the event’s recency (0-3-year window) the Time Decay Principle permits elevated scores; snippets that evidence direct, realised financial impact or name critical operational choke-points rate highest, while generic or strongly mitigated statements score lower.
